profile.reading:
This 184,553-square-foot building at 1001 Windward Concourse in Alpharetta, Georgia is a purpose-built data center owned by Mapletree Industrial Trust, a Singapore-listed real estate investment trust managed by Mapletree Investments, itself a global real estate firm wholly owned by Temasek Holdings, the Singapore state investment company. Mapletree entered the U.S. data-center market in December 2017, when Mapletree Redwood Data Centre Trust -- a joint venture between Mapletree Investments and Mapletree Industrial Trust -- acquired a 14-property, roughly $750 million data-center portfolio from Carter Validus Mission Critical REIT, an Alpharetta specialist in net-leased mission-critical real estate. At the time of that sale the portfolio was reported as 97 percent occupied across 15 tenants, though the seller did not break out occupancy or lease terms for individual buildings. This Alpharetta property was one of the assets in that transaction, and Mapletree's own property listing continues to identify it by this address as part of its industrial and data-center holdings. Public commercial listings and a local business directory entry associate an IBM-branded operation with this address, consistent with the building functioning as a leased, single- or multi-tenant enterprise data center rather than a Mapletree-operated colocation facility for the open market; Mapletree, as a REIT landlord, typically owns the building and leases the technical space to an operating tenant rather than running IT services itself. Neither Mapletree nor any identified tenant publishes power capacity, cooling design, or certification details for this specific building, which is standard practice for net-leased, single-tenant data center real estate where the operating tenant controls disclosure of its own infrastructure. Alpharetta, in the northern Atlanta metro along the Windward Parkway corridor, has developed into a secondary Atlanta-area data center and corporate-campus cluster, and this building sits within that broader concentration of enterprise office and technical-space development north of the city.

Mapletree Industrial Trust is one of three Singapore-listed real estate investment trusts managed under the broader Mapletree Investments platform, which together with the group's private-equity real estate funds oversees a global portfolio spanning logistics, office, retail, industrial, data-center, student-housing, and residential assets across roughly a dozen markets, including a meaningful U.S. data-center segment built up through acquisitions like the 2017 Carter Validus portfolio purchase that brought this Alpharetta property into the trust. For a REIT of this kind, a fully leased, single-tenant data-center building such as this one functions as a long-duration, contracted-income asset rather than an operating business the trust actively runs day to day -- the trust's public disclosures accordingly focus on portfolio-level occupancy, rental income, and lease-expiry schedules rather than building-by-building technical specifications, which is standard practice across net-leased data-center real estate and is why no power, cooling, or capacity figures are published for this specific address.

reading.body:
Mapletree Industrial operates 184,553 square feet of technical space in Alpharetta but publishes no power capacity, so its role in Georgia's AI infrastructure cannot be sized.

The operator's public specification sheet lists only floor area. Power consumption, cooling architecture, and structural capacity determine whether a data center supports dense GPU clusters or lighter workloads, but none of these are disclosed. Without megawatt figures, this facility cannot be ranked against peers or evaluated for AI suitability. It is large enough to matter if the supporting infrastructure exists, but that condition is unstated.

Georgia has 33 mapped data center facilities overall. Only two publish power capacity, totaling 42 MW. This Alpharetta campus falls outside that measurable set. Absence from capacity rankings reflects missing data rather than confirmed size. A buyer or operator assessing this location would need to request power capacity, cooling specifications, and compliance certifications directly from Mapletree Industrial Trust.
